_comment: What installer/notices.py cannot read off a package: the runtime and native
parts that arrive with no wheel of their own, the few components that ship no
notice text, and the written offer each copyleft licence asks for. Everything
else -- every wheel of python/requirements.lock and every crate of Cargo.lock --
is gathered from the build's own files, so it is not repeated here.
A 'from_path' is relative to sys.base_prefix, the Python this venv was made
from; a 'from_wheel' names a wheel whose notice files belong to a component
that is not itself shipped as a library. 'terms' answers the gate for a
component that carries no text, by name. An 'offer' covers a family through

components.name: Python
components.what: the interpreter and its standard library, frozen into both executables (python314.dll, base_library.zip and the modules beside them). Its LICENSE.txt also carries the notices of the software Python itself incorporates

components.name: Tcl/Tk
components.what: the classic window's toolkit: tcl86t.dll, tk86t.dll, _tkinter.pyd and the script folders beside them (_tcl_data, _tk_data, tcl8), which overtone-py.exe opens the Tk window with. The web shell window does not use it

components.name: PyInstaller bootloader
components.what: the loader at the head of Overtone.exe and overtone-py.exe: the only part of PyInstaller that ships. Its own exception permits a frozen application under any licence, and the hooks and the build tool stay on the build machine

components.name: Microsoft Visual C++ runtime
components.what: VCRUNTIME140.dll and VCRUNTIME140_1.dll, which PyInstaller copies beside Python; overtone-cli.exe links the same runtime, which is why it sits in _internal rather than beside Overtone.exe
components.terms: redistributable with an application under the Visual Studio licence terms that ship with the toolchain that built it; Microsoft supplies no notice file to copy, and the terms are at the address above

components.name: Microsoft Edge WebView2
components.licence: Microsoft Software License Terms (Edge WebView2 SDK)
components.what: Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.dll, Microsoft.Web.WebView2.WinForms.dll and WebView2Loader.dll, which arrive inside the pywebview wheel and are what the app's window is. The WebView2 runtime itself is part of Windows and is not bundled: a machine without it gets an error, never a download
components.terms: redistributable with an application under the Microsoft Software License Terms for the Edge WebView2 SDK, at the address above; the SDK ships no notice file to copy

terms.clr-loader: MIT, as the LICENSE text below says in full; the wheel's own metadata declares no licence, which is why it is named here
terms.proxy-tools: MIT, by the wheel's own classifier (Jonathan Tushman, http://github.com/jtushman/proxy_tools); the wheel ships no licence file, so there is no text to copy
terms.realfft: MIT, as Cargo.toml declares; the published crate carries no licence file, so there is no text to copy (https://github.com/HEnquist/realfft)

offers.title: libsndfile, through the soundfile wheel -- LGPL-2.1-or-later
offers.text:
What ships: _internal\_soundfile_data\libsndfile_x64.dll, the build that
comes inside soundfile 0.14.0 as installed from PyPI. Neither it nor soundfile
is modified here; its COPYING is reproduced in full further down.

The LGPL asks that you be able to use a libsndfile of your own instead. You
can: the DLL is a separate file in the program folder and soundfile opens it
by name at run time, so a build of your own put in its place is the one that
runs. No relinking of Overtone is needed.

The source: https://github.com/libsndfile/libsndfile, and the soundfile
release the DLL came in, source archive included, at
https://pypi.org/project/soundfile/0.14.0/#files

If both of those are gone and the exact source used here is wanted, ask at
https://github.com/githaltwastaken/Overtone/issues and it will be provided.

offers.title: libsoxr, through the soxr wheel -- LGPL-2.1-or-later
offers.text:
What ships: _internal\soxr\soxr_ext.pyd, the extension module of soxr 1.1.0 as
installed from PyPI, which has libsoxr linked into it statically. Neither is
modified here; COPYING.LGPL and LICENSE-libsoxr.txt are reproduced in full
further down.

Statically linked means replacing libsoxr means rebuilding that one module,
not Overtone: the sources are
https://github.com/dofuuz/python-soxr (the wheel, version 1.1.0) and
https://sourceforge.net/projects/soxr/ (libsoxr), and the wheel's own source
archive is at https://pypi.org/project/soxr/1.1.0/#files

Overtone loads soxr through librosa, as a resampler. If the exact source used
here is wanted and those addresses are gone, ask at
https://github.com/githaltwastaken/Overtone/issues and it will be provided.

offers.title: certifi -- MPL-2.0
offers.text:
certifi is a CA certificate bundle that arrives through requests, which
arrives through pooch, which arrives through librosa. Overtone makes no
network call of any kind, so nothing in the app ever reads it; it ships
because it is in the dependency tree, and it is listed because it is there.

Unmodified, as installed from PyPI. The MPL asks that the source of its
covered files be available: https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi and
https://pypi.org/project/certifi/2026.7.22/#files

offers.title: Symphonia (fifteen crates) -- MPL-2.0
offers.text:
Symphonia is the Rust engine's decoder: it reads the MP3, FLAC, Ogg, WAV, MP4
and Matroska files Overtone analyses, linked into overtone-cli.exe. Every
crate of it is version 0.6.1 as published on crates.io, unmodified, and each
one's licence text is reproduced further down.

The MPL asks that the source of its covered files be available:
https://github.com/pdeljanov/Symphonia, and crates.io keeps the exact
published archive of every version, e.g.
https://crates.io/crates/symphonia-core/0.6.1

offers.title: PyInstaller's bootloader -- GPL-2.0 with the bootloader exception
offers.text:
PyInstaller is GPLv2, with an exception for exactly this case: the bootloader
it puts at the head of a frozen executable may be distributed inside an
application under any licence, and does not make that application GPL. The
exception's own wording is in PyInstaller's COPYING.txt, reproduced further
down.

Only the bootloader ships. PyInstaller itself, its hooks and its build
machinery stay on the build machine (installer/requirements-build.lock).

The source: https://github.com/pyinstaller/pyinstaller and
https://pypi.org/project/pyinstaller/6.22.3/#files
